newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle close higher ahead of report.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle close higher ahead of report.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed higher ahead of the monthly USDA Cattle-on-Feed report. Feeder cattle also showed evening up but were pressured by higher corn futures to close lower, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.375 to 0.050 higher with April up most at 68.700 cents. Feeder cattle ended off 0.100 to 0.575 with May off 0.450 at 68.150 cents.
Mixed short covering and position squaring dominated live cattle futures trade much of the session. Unwinding of bear spreads ahead of the report added to support in the nearby, traders said.

An easier tone to boxed beef and cash cattle markets provided only little resistance early as trader attention turned to the report. Some cash cattle traded $1 per cwt lower at $67 and heavy-weight choice boxed beef has been trending lower, they said.
Heavy-weight beef, at $101.74, is at its lowest price level since February 24 and down $6.25 since March 4.

Analyst estimates on the USDA Cattle-on-Feed report ranged from 105 to 107.5 percent of a year ago for on-feed supplies at the major 7-state feedlot areas as of March 1 and averaged 106.5 percent. February placements averaged 104.2 in a range of 99 to 110 percent and marketings averaged 97.9 in a a range of 94 to 99 percent.

Feeder cattle futures remained pressured from higher corn futures, but trade was slow at times as traders squared positions ahead of the report. A lower CME feeder cattle index also weighed on the market early but had little effect later in the day, traders added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.17 at $68.48 per cwt.
